Issued at 255 AM CDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Current conditions early this morning across the forecast feature 
partly to mostly cloudy skies and temperatures mainly in the 30s. 
Low level cloud cover has been thickening across Nebraska and has 
been shifting into far southern SD. Surface high pressure centered 
across the Dakotas this morning will have a temporary hold on 
weather conditions today across parts of our forecast area. However, 
changes are in the works as an upper level low across the Four 
Corners region today sends shortwave energy northward across the 
Plains. This will aid in an influx of moisture northward into our 
southern zones during the morning and midday hours. With the sfc 
ridge positioned to our north and northeast, and a dry northeast 
fetch into our northern zones, this should keep most of the rainfall 
across our south through the first half of the day. BUFKIT soundings 
across northeast SD indicates low level dry air persisting through 
midday. The lower portion of the atmospheric column begins to 
saturate during the afternoon hours when more favorable mid level 
dynamics or UVM becomes stronger. CAMs more or less agree on this 
scenario with most of the rainfall concentrated to the south through 
the morning before becoming more widespread during the course of the 
afternoon into this evening. Although temperatures will remain 
rather cool today into tonight, p-types across the forecast area 
remain mostly liquid per the latest EC ENS p-type meteograms. Models 
begin to disperse the widespread precip coverage later tonight into 
the overnight hours.

That upper low is progged to shift northeast across the Rockies 
tonight and out into the Central and Northern Plains Monday into 
Monday night. Another slug of more significant moisture shifts north 
into our region. Some of the moisture within this upper low has 
eastern Pacific origins from remnants of a tropical system. Some 
noteworthy rainfall from this system is expected to fall in parts of 
the forecast area. Probabilities of seeing at least 1 inch or more 
between today and early Tuesday range from 20-50 percent across 
north central SD to 50-90 percent from south central SD into 
northeast SD and west central MN. At this point, along and east of a 
Pierre to Aberdeen line have at least a 70 percent chance or higher 
of seeing that amount of precipitation. Again, the precipitation 
type across most of the forecast area will fall as rain per the p-
type meteograms, albeit a chilly rain. However, there are some 
caveats to this that could lead to our first bout of snowfall this 
season. Timing and placement of the mid and upper low features along 
with the temperature profile, specifically the strength and depth of 
a warm nose aloft and near sfc temperatures and moisture or lack 
thereof in the DGZ will dictate if/when and where snow may occur. 
Most favorable areas where these ingredients may all come together 
for frozen precip will be across north central SD. P-type meteograms 
at MBG indicate a 10-30 percent probability of seeing wet snow 
Monday afternoon/evening. Again timing and placement of precip and 
temperatures will be key to any accumulation possibility. 
Probabilities of seeing 1 inch of accumulation range from 30-60 
percent and confined to mainly western Corson County. The intensity 
of any falling snow plus ground temperatures will be factors 
if and where snow will stick.

This system will exit to our northeast early Tuesday and quickly be 
followed up with another upper trough that is currently progged to 
take a track more to our northwest from MT into ND. If this 
verifies, our area should remain mostly on the dry side around the 
middle of the week. Sfc and upper ridging mid to late week should 
lead to drier conditions and modifying temperatures at or above 
normal for late October.
